title: Post-Quantum Security and Cryptographic Migration knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best summarizes the main idea of Post-Quantum Security and Cryptographic Migration?
options: Post-quantum migration starts with a cryptographic inventory, data lifetime and exposure analysis, vendor-support checks, interoperability planning, and controlled transition tests. The lesson distinguishes finalized standards from experimental approaches and does not claim that every current system is immediately broken.
A single successful test proves that a system is completely secure in every environment.
The fastest workflow is always to skip evidence collection and make changes directly in production.
Security responsibilities disappear when a technical tool has been installed.
questions.answer_key: Post-quantum migration starts with a cryptographic inventory, data lifetime and exposure analysis, vendor-support checks, interoperability planning, and controlled transition tests. The lesson distinguishes finalized standards from experimental approaches and does not claim that every current system is immediately broken.
questions.explanation: The lesson's core idea is: Post-quantum migration starts with a cryptographic inventory, data lifetime and exposure analysis, vendor-support checks, interoperability planning, and controlled transition tests. The lesson distinguishes finalized standards from experimental approaches and does not claim that every current system is immediately broken. The other options overstate what one test or tool can prove and ignore the need for context, evidence, and governance.

questions.prompt: You are applying Post-Quantum Security and Cryptographic Migration to a new scenario. What is the best first step?
options: Define scope and expected behavior, collect relevant evidence, and verify the result in an authorized or synthetic environment.
Repeat the same test against unrelated public systems to collect more data.
Disable useful logging so the test output looks simpler.
Assume an unfamiliar result proves malicious intent without corroboration.
questions.answer_key: Define scope and expected behavior, collect relevant evidence, and verify the result in an authorized or synthetic environment.
questions.explanation: Bound the work, define expected behavior, and collect relevant evidence in a safe and authorized context before drawing conclusions.

questions.prompt: Which practice most improves the reliability of work on Post-Quantum Security and Cryptographic Migration?
options: Document assumptions and limitations, then select a proportionate defensive next step based on evidence and current guidance.
Publish raw secrets and personal information so someone else can reproduce the test.
Treat a teaching example as proof of production security without retesting.
Skip documenting exceptions because they make the report more complicated.
questions.answer_key: Document assumptions and limitations, then select a proportionate defensive next step based on evidence and current guidance.
questions.explanation: Security claims should be backed by reproducible evidence and clear limits; sensitive information must be protected and production-specific assumptions checked.
